forces-poids-caisse-etabli.scenario: A 5.0 kg toolbox sits still on the lab workbench, where the strength of gravity is g = 9.81 m/s².
forces-poids-caisse-etabli.question: What is the weight of this toolbox?
forces-poids-caisse-etabli.explanation: Weight is the force of gravity pulling on an object: P = m · g, with m in kilograms and g in m/s². Here P = 5.0 × 9.81 = 49.05 N, so about 49.1 N. Mass (5.0 kg) and weight (49.1 N) are two different things: the mass stays the same on any planet or moon, but the weight does not.

forces-soutien-plan-incline.scenario: A 20 kg crate stays still on a ramp tilted 30° from the horizontal. A small stop block fixed at the bottom of the slope keeps it from sliding.
forces-soutien-plan-incline.question: What is the support force of the ramp on the crate (g = 9.81 m/s²)?
forces-soutien-plan-incline.explanation: The support force always pushes at a right angle to the surface. So it only balances the part of the weight that presses into the ramp: N = m · g · cos α. Here P = 20 × 9.81 = 196.2 N, then N = 196.2 × cos 30° = 169.9 N, so about 170 N. The support force equals the weight only on a horizontal surface (α = 0°). The other part of the weight, m · g · sin α = 98.1 N, is held back by the stop block.

forces-archimede-cube-flottant.scenario: A wooden cube with 20 cm sides and a mass of 4.8 kg floats in an aquarium, with part of the cube sticking out of the water.
forces-archimede-cube-flottant.question: What is the buoyant force of the water on this cube (ρ_water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.81 m/s²)?
forces-archimede-cube-flottant.explanation: The buoyant force only depends on the volume that is really underwater: F_A = ρ_water · g · V_submerged. The cube floats without moving, so F_A balances its weight: F_A = P = 4.8 × 9.81 = 47.1 N. This means V_submerged = 4.8 / 1000 = 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³, which is 60% of the cube's 8.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Using the whole volume would give 1000 × 9.81 × 8.0 × 10⁻³ = 78.5 N, a value you only get if you push the whole cube under the water.
